look_here_first: LOOK FOR A LONG DENSE BOTTLEBRUSH PANICLE and BROAD HAIRY LEAVES: a relatively coarse perennial grass often found on shaded limestone slopes or canyon edges in the Edwards Plateau. Each spikelet commonly has a LONG bristle (rudimentary branch); the head is much longer and more densely bristled than S. reverchonii.

best_field_traits: Coarse warm-season perennial bunchgrass with rhizomatous/rooted base, often fairly tall, sometimes exceeding 1 m.
Relatively broad, pubescent foliage with prominent midvein, often about 5–18 mm wide.
Conspicuous elongate single terminal bottlebrush-like flowering head; Texas A&M describes inflorescence about 15–35 cm long.
Spikelets generally about 2.1–2.6 mm in regional treatments, often associated with a single conspicuous long bristle.
Bristles are sterile reduced branchlets NOT a true awn of the floret; study both bristle and tiny spikelet.
Edwards Plateau limestone canyons/open woods and partially shaded areas are useful habitat cues, not proof of species or county nativity.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full erect clump in shaded limestone habitat and head side profile
Long panicle with ruler (top, midpoint, bottom)
One basal bristle and its attached spikelet together, macro ruler
Broad pubescent blade with ruler and prominent midvein
True leaf collar ligule and perennial basal rooting system
crew_field_check: Count bristles under 10× magnification; these are reduced branches, NOT true awns.
Measure whole flowering head and a mature spikelet.
Inspect the base/collar/rhizomes on the SAME PLANT; do not force identification from a single image.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. reverchonii is more slender with short sparse/absent bristles and typically an interrupted flowerhead. S. parviflora has a short dense head and many bristles per spikelet plus a short knotty rhizome. Millet S. italica is annual and often very robust with a cultivated densely seeded foxtail, not the same native perennial ecological form.
